representation_fit.evidence: Brief: verb 'complete' on a single high-consequence workflow, hierarchy=high, density=low, comparison/spatiality=none, seed 'irreversible steps have recovery/confirmation paths'. The impl is exactly that shape: a release runbook console for one object (the 14-step orders-api v2.4.0 flow, source/data.js:3-212) with a 6-phase hierarchy (data.js:10-17), one step on screen at a time, no comparison/spatial views; the medium-uncertainty facet is modeled by randomized gate metrics (data.js:91,133,173 'badChance') requiring judgment.

primary_task_salience.evidence: Initial screen in both screenshots/1280x860.png and screenshots/1440x900.png puts the current workflow step center-stage ('核对变更单与发布窗口' with its 2 checkboxes), the full 14-step path in the left rail with the active step highlighted (app.js:157-181), and progress '0/14' plus a '零失误' badge top-right (index.html:25-32): walking the flow with zero mistakes dominates the first screen.

time_to_understand.evidence: Top bar states what/where immediately (发布指挥台 · orders-api v2.4.0 · runbook RLB-2.4, index.html:13-18; change/window/approval chips index.html:20-24); center pane carries an explicit crumb '阶段 预检准备 · p0-1 · 预计 2 分钟' (app.js:244) and a plain stop-condition instruction (data.js:22). Both viewports render the same clean grid; text.truncation check passes (measurement-summary.json:11).

navigation_cost.evidence: The primary object is on the initial screen — zero navigation. Advancing is a single in-place click per item (toggle-check → completeStep, app.js:471-478); future steps are locked until predecessors complete (app.js:170) and previewed as '接下来' chips (app.js:305-312); any unlocked step is viewable with one rail click without leaving the page (app.js:466-470).

context_loss.evidence: Single-page shared state: checks, actions, gate verdicts, and the typed-phrase confirm modal (app.js:518-533) all mutate one step list and re-render in place; recovery paths open as inline <details> inside the stage (app.js:205-238, 317-328); modal cancel records nothing and returns to the same step (index.html:56, app.js:517); left rail and right status rail persist through every action.

ui_surface_complexity.evidence: Four permanent surfaces (topbar, phase rail, stage, 4-panel status rail; index.html:12-39) each serve the zero-mistake job — environment snapshot, irreversible-step tracker (app.js:356-364), mistake log, operation log. Only 2 controls are visible at start (1280x860.png). Minor redundancy: mistake count appears three times (badge index.html:30, stage footer app.js:302, 失误记录 panel app.js:367-378).

accessibility.evidence: Receipt: a11y.contrast=fail, a11y.target_size=fail, a11y.focus_order=pass (measurement-summary.json:13-15), plus type.min_projected_size=fail (measurement-summary.json:16). Source corroborates: 18x18px checkbox targets (.task-box, styles.css:190-196); pervasive low-contrast faint/muted tokens on near-black (styles.css:10-11, used at styles.css:124, 158, 289, 354); widespread 10.5-11.5px type (styles.css:158, 324, 354). Mitigating: semantic buttons/details, role=dialog aria-modal (index.html:44), aria-live toasts (index.html:41), which is consistent with focus_order passing.

frontend_rework.evidence: No visible layout defects: layout.overflow, layout.responsive_collision, text.truncation all pass (measurement-summary.json:10-12) and both screenshots show a clean three-column grid at 1280x860 and 1440x900. But 3 of 7 receipt checks fail (a11y.contrast, a11y.target_size, type.min_projected_size; measurement-summary.json:4-5, 13-16), implying a styling rework pass; one trivial code smell (no-op replace, app.js:172).

acceptance_seed_coverage.evidence: Seed 'irreversible steps have recovery/confirmation paths' is covered on both levels. Confirmation: p3-1/p4-1 tagged 不可逆 (data.js:109,150; rail tag app.js:174) and require typed phrases MIGRATE-217/CUTOVER (data.js:113,154) in a modal whose exec button stays disabled until the phrase matches (app.js:410-424, 537-543), with cancel leaving no record (index.html:56). Recovery: concrete per-step paths (reverse fix script / snapshot restore, data.js:116-124; Kill-Switch 回切, data.js:157-165), tracked as 恢复路径未查阅/已查阅 in the right rail (app.js:361), prompted '建议先查阅' before execution (app.js:297), reminded after execution (app.js:293); and correct recovery handling is explicitly not counted as a mistake (app.js:132-135), reinforcing the zero-mistake success standard.

defects_observed: a11y.contrast fail: faint/muted text on near-black used for phase intents, step numbers, log timestamps, footers (styles.css:10-11; applied at styles.css:124, 158, 289, 354)
a11y.target_size fail: 18x18px checkbox targets (.task-box, styles.css:190-196) and small chips/badges
Minor redundancy: mistake count rendered in three places (index.html:30; app.js:302; app.js:367-378)
Trivial code smell: no-op st.id.replace('-','-') at app.js:172
scores.overall_note: impl-03 is a release runbook console whose representation matches the brief's consequential-flow shape almost exactly: one 14-step workflow across 6 phases, a single step on screen at a time, randomized gate metrics carrying the medium-uncertainty facet, and a top-level zero-mistake verdict (app.js:427-456). The acceptance seed is addressed structurally — typed-phrase confirmation modals (MIGRATE-217, CUTOVER) and explicit per-step recovery paths that are tracked ('未查阅/已查阅') and encouraged before execution — and incentive-wise, since correct recovery handling is explicitly not penalized as a mistake (app.js:132-135). All data is inline with no network requests (data.js:1-2; app.js:553-556), so the first screen is usable at load, and navigation/context costs are minimal because every action happens in place on one persistent page. The observable weaknesses align with the three failed receipt checks — low-contrast faint text, 18px checkbox targets, and pervasive sub-12px type — while all three layout checks pass and both screenshots show no visible defects. Task completion time, information retrieval accuracy, and human preference are not observable in this package, and the understandability score is a model-judged label proxy, not a human measurement.
